# Perception Skills — Shared Reference

> Not a skill (no `SKILL.md`, so the manifest scanner ignores it). Read by `perception-investigate-attack`, `perception-triage-alert`, `perception-protect-against-threat`, `perception-extract-threat-intel` and `perception-tune-detection` so the common rules live in one place.
> **PII-free:** keep tenant GUIDs, UPNs, session IDs and article IDs out of this file.

Microsoft Perception is an **optional** agentic-security system in the Defender portal. These skills drive it through the **Perception MCP** (`perception-mcp-*` tools). Everything here degrades gracefully when Perception isn't configured.

---

## 1. Preconditions (every Perception skill, first step)

1. **Detect the MCP.** Look for tools whose names start with `perception-mcp-` (`list_playbooks`, `start_session`, `list_sessions`, `get_session`, `list_agent_runs`, `get_agent_run`, `get_agent_run_messages`, `get_session_summary`, `list_outputs`, `read_output`, `stop_session`). **The tool surface has changed between Perception MCP versions** (earlier builds had `get_session_overview`, `get_conversation_activity` and `send_message`; the published Learn contract has exactly the 11 tools listed here, and although its overview says runs can be continued with additional instructions there is **no tool for it**, so do not promise follow-up guidance to a running session: ask the user to continue it in the Defender portal); trust the tool definitions you actually have loaded over this list, and call `list_playbooks` for the current playbook catalog and input schema. Many are deferred — use the tool search tool to load them. If none exist (after a tool search for deferred `perception-mcp-*` tools): **give the setup guidance below as the first thing in your answer** and never start, poll or re-validate anything. Do not fake results. **Offline read-only mode:** if `temp/perception_sessions.json` or `reports/perception/` already holds a saved result for the requested input, you may *offer* it after the guidance, clearly labeled *"saved result, not re-validated — Perception MCP unavailable"* and `[asserted]`. In this mode do **not** write or edit any report, do **not** post a Mission Control finding, do **not** update the index, and do not recommend follow-ups that depend on fresh Perception data. If nothing is saved, stop after the guidance.

   **Setup guidance (use when the MCP is missing):**
   > The Perception MCP isn't configured in this session. To use this skill, add an HTTP MCP server pointing at `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp` (for example in `.mcp.json` / `.vscode/mcp.json`: `"perception-mcp": { "type": "http", "url": "https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp" }`), sign in when prompted, then reload MCP servers and retry. You need Microsoft Perception enabled in your tenant (Defender portal → Perception) and a Security Reader role or higher.
   >
   > Docs: [What is Perception MCP?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/agentic-security/agentic-security-mcp) and the [tools reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/agentic-security/agentic-security-mcp-tools-contract) (published 2026-11-19). The documented endpoint is `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp` (HTTP, tools `*`); verified end to end on 2026-11-20 (same 11 tools, same tool schemas, same session and output data as the earlier `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp` endpoint, which also answered and is the legacy URL). Prerequisites per the docs: tenant onboarding (Perception is in **Limited Public Preview**, invitation-only), Defender URBAC across all workloads, and **Security Reader** (Security Admin sets up agents). Sample prompts and Entra/agent-identity scoping notes are on the same docs pages. Copilot CLI: `/mcp add` with Server Name `perception-mcp`, Type HTTP, URL `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp`, Tools `*` (matches this repo's templates); VS Code: *MCP: Add Server* → HTTP → the same URL.
2. **State the active tenant** (read `tenant_id` from `config.json`; match to `config.json.<name>` if present) before any tenant-scoped call. Perception runs against whatever tenant the MCP is authenticated to — if that could differ from `config.json`, say so.
3. **Ask before starting a session.** A session consumes agent capacity, is **billed by Perception** (separate from Copilot AI credits) and runs in the tenant under the agent's own identity. State the playbook, the exact input, the expected runtime **and the estimated Perception cost range** (snapshot of the portal's *Estimate Costs* page, USD per agent outcome: `investigate-incident` ≈ $2.69–$18.82; `proactive-protection` ≈ $209–$527 for its four reports — TI $3.89–$6.80, Recon $87.50–$325.00, Detection $63.00–$95.37, Posture $55.00–$99.64; `analyze-article` ≈ $3.89–$6.80 — snapshot 2026-11-19; Microsoft says these are not a quote and actual costs may be higher; check the portal for current numbers); wait for a yes. Reusing an existing finished session costs nothing on the Perception side and needs no confirmation beyond offering it.
4. **Read-only playbooks only — this is a hard refusal, not a prompt.** If asked to run, "test", "scan" or "pen test" a web app/domain, or for any playbook not on the allow-list, **refuse in your first reply**: do not call `list_playbooks`/`start_session`, do not ask for a target domain or confirmation, say that active testing playbooks are blocked by these skills (they must be launched by a human in the Defender portal), and offer the nearest read-only option (e.g. `prioritize-posture` / `proactive-protection`). Allowed: `investigate-incident`, `triage-security-copilot`, `analyze-article`, `proactive-protection`, `prioritize-posture`. **Never** start `red-web-pentest` or `find-fix-web-app-security-risks` (active testing) from these skills.

## 2. Starting a session (`start_session`)

**Portal names (use these when talking to the user and in card prompts):** `investigate-incident` = *Investigate attack*; `proactive-protection` = *Protect against a threat*; `analyze-article` = *Extract threat intelligence*; `detect-emerging-threats` = *Detect emerging threats* (portal only, not startable via MCP); `triage-security-copilot` = *Triage alert*. Others seen in `list_playbooks`: `prioritize-posture` = *Plan for posture remediation*, `run-reconnaissance` = *Identify attack paths*, `assess-identity-risk` = *Assess identity risks*, `red-web-pentest` = *Run web pen test* and `find-fix-web-app-security-risks` = *Protect web app* (the last two are active testing: always refused, §1.4). Microsoft Learn (Key concepts, 2026-11-20) also lists *Reduce credential phishing risk* and *Close identity attack paths used in your environment* (Identity Risk Reduction Agent: Conditional Access recommendations); they were not in this tenant's catalog and are **not** on the allow-list, so skills do not start them. The catalog is read-only and grows over time: always trust `list_playbooks` over this list. Use the `uniqueName` for API calls and the portal name in prose.

1. Call **`list_playbooks`** first. `playbookId` is the playbook's **GUID `id`** from that result (match on `uniqueName`, e.g. `investigate-incident`); **do not pass `uniqueName`** and do not hard-code GUIDs (they come from the tool version in use).
2. Build `inputs` from the playbook's `triggers[].inputs[]` — an **array** of items `{"key", "type", "values":[...], "displayName"?, "entityUrl"?}`:
   - `key` = the input `key` exactly; `type` = one of its `acceptedInputTypes`; `values` = non-empty array of strings. `entityUrl` is optional: an absolute `https://` link without credentials for a **single** entity (omit it when passing several `values`).
   - Respect `required`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, `displayNameRequired`, `allowedValues`, `dependencies`.

| Playbook (`uniqueName`) | `inputs` |
|---|---|
| `investigate-incident` | `[{"key":"incidentOrAlert","type":"defenderIncidentId","values":["<incident id>"]}]` (`defenderAlertId` for an alert) |
| `triage-security-copilot` | `[{"key":"triage-alert","type":"defenderTriageAlertId","values":["<Defender alert id>"],"displayName":"<alert title> - <alert id>"}]` (the portal also records `entityUrl:"/alerts/<id>"`; the input accepts an alert ID or URL; Sentinel `SystemAlertId` is not an alert ID here) |
| `proactive-protection` / `analyze-article`, internal article | `[{"key":"article","type":"defenderThreatIntelligenceId","values":["<article id>"],"displayName":"<exact title>"}]` — `displayName` is **required** |
| `proactive-protection` / `analyze-article`, external article | `[{"key":"article","type":"defenderThreatIntelligenceId","values":["<https URL>"]}]` (no `displayName`); the form `values:["EXTERNAL"]` + `displayName:"<URL>"` is also accepted |

Observed behavior with **external URLs** (mixed): the `ic3.gov/…/261113.csv` URL produced a full `proactive-protection` run (TI + detection reports); the `.pdf` variants of the same advisory finished with only an audit log or a TI report and **no detection report**; the Microsoft Security Blog URL failed (the agent reported it could not access the article and advised retrying in a few minutes), while the **internal ID + title** form for that same article succeeded. So prefer the internal form when known; retry a URL once after a few minutes; if only a URL exists, run `analyze-article` first (≈ 4 min) as a cheap viability check before the ≈ 1 h `proactive-protection` run. External-URL sessions record `value: "EXTERNAL"` in `tags`/`inputs`, so match them on `inputs[].displayName` / `entityUrl`.

**Start requirements (Microsoft Learn: Perception get started / Playbooks):** the caller needs the **Security Reader** role *and* **Run** access to every agent the playbook uses, and a playbook is only active when all its agents are set up and enabled (a Security Admin does that in the Defender portal: Perception → Agents). If `start_session` is rejected for permissions or an agent that is not set up, report exactly that, point the user to the portal setup, and **do not retry** or switch to another playbook on your own.

`start_session` returns `201` with the new **session id** and an initial `agentRuns` snapshot immediately; the work is asynchronous. A failed/timed-out call may still have created a session — **check `list_sessions` before retrying** to avoid duplicates.

## 3. Session lookup — "has this already been run?"

`list_sessions` returns the same compact record as `get_session`, newest-created first, default page 15 (max 100), with an optional **`filter` on `status` / `statusDetail` only** (e.g. `status eq 'succeeded'`, `statusDetail eq 'waitingForInput'`). There is **no filter on input or playbook**, but each record now carries structured data you can match **exactly** (no title parsing):

| Field | Example | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `tags` | `playbookId=investigate-incident`, `input:incident=<incident-id>`, `input:threat-intelligence=<id or EXTERNAL>`, `playbookId=triage-security-copilot` + `input:triage-alert=<alert-id>` (+ `method:Manual` or `method:Automatic`) | match playbook + input |
| `inputs[]` | `{type:"defenderIncidentId", value:"<incident-id>"}`; external article: `value:"EXTERNAL"`, `displayName:"<URL>"` | confirm the input; for external articles match on `displayName`/`entityUrl` |
| `status` / `statusDetail` | `succeeded`·`completed`, `running`·`inProgress`, `failed`, `running`·`waitingForInput`, `…`·`stopped` | pick reusable runs |
| `webUrl`, `initiatedBy`, `createdAt` | | link, who ran it, age |

Neither the incident nor Advanced Hunting shows a back-reference to a Perception session, so look up in this order:

1. **Local index** `temp/perception_sessions.json` (gitignored). Array of `{kind, key, sessionId, playbook, startedAt, status, reportPath}`. Written by these skills at `start_session`. Check it first.
2. **Scan `list_sessions` — follow `continuationToken` until you hit the boundary. Reading one page is never enough.** Use `pageSize` 100 (add `filter: status eq 'succeeded'` when you only want reusable runs). Per page, match `tags` (`playbookId=<uniqueName>` **and** `input:…=<value>`). Keep requesting the next page (pass the returned `continuationToken` unchanged, with the same `pageSize` and `filter`) until **either**:
   - **Boundary reached:** the *oldest* `createdAt` on the page is older than the input's creation time (an investigation cannot predate its incident; an article run can't predate the article). Only then is "no match" a real answer; or
   - **Cap reached:** 10 pages (1,000 sessions), or no `continuationToken` is returned.
   Pages are large (≈ 30 KB each) and get saved to a temp file — parse each page with PowerShell/Python (filter on `tags`, track the oldest `createdAt`) instead of reading them into chat.
   Page 1 covering only a day or two in a busy tenant is **normal, not a stopping point** (observed: 4 pages × 100 sessions ≈ 3.5 days).
3. Discard **unusable sessions**: `status` ≠ `succeeded`, or a succeeded session whose `list_outputs` has no real report (see §5). `list_agent_runs` shows which agents ran — a run with only the Main Agent is a stub.
4. Multiple runs per input are normal (including runs started by other users — `initiatedBy`). Show the candidates (status, createdAt, initiator) and let the user choose reuse vs fresh run.
5. **Report the scan honestly.** Always state how far the scan went: pages read, sessions checked, oldest `createdAt` reached, and why you stopped (*boundary reached* / *cap reached* / *no more pages*). Say *"no matching Perception session exists"* only after the **boundary** was reached; if you stopped at the **cap**, say *"none found in the most recent N sessions (back to <createdAt>) — an older run can't be ruled out"*. Never use the "can't be ruled out" caveat after reading only the first page. The local index is what makes lookups for older inputs reliable.
6. **URL input with no usable match → title fallback (always confirmed, never silent).** A session records the *input it was started with*: an article run started from an internal Activity Profile ID has the ID and title but **not** the article's public URL, so a URL lookup can miss a perfectly good run. When the input is an `https://` article URL and the exact URL match (`inputs[].displayName` / `entityUrl`) yields **no usable session** (none found, or every match is unusable per step 3):
   1. Fetch the page (web fetch) and take its title (`<title>`/first heading; drop a site suffix such as `| Microsoft Security Blog`). If the fetch fails or no clear title is found, skip the fallback and say so.
   2. Normalize both sides: lowercase, strip the profile prefix (`Activity Profile:`, `Threat Overview Profile:`, `Vulnerability Profile:`, `Actor Profile:`), remove punctuation, collapse whitespace. A **title match** = the normalized page title equals the normalized session `displayName` / `inputs[].displayName` (or one fully contains the other). Topical or keyword similarity is **not** a match.
   3. Collect title matches in the same paging pass as step 2 (same boundary/cap) and apply the usability filter from step 3.
   4. Present them as **"probable same article — matched by title, not by URL"** with status, createdAt, initiator and usability, plus the URL-match results you rejected and why. **Ask the user to confirm** before using one; tag the evidence `title-matched` so the provenance stays visible. Never substitute silently, and never start a run on the strength of a title match alone — reuse is offered, a fresh run still needs the usual confirmation.

### 3.7 Local session cache (the MCP cannot search sessions)

`list_sessions` filters only on `status` / `statusDetail`; there is no text, playbook, date or article filter. For "what has Perception already produced?" questions use the helper [`session_cache.py`](session_cache.py): an incremental, gitignored cache (`temp/perception_session_cache.json`) of every session seen — id, playbook, status, createdAt, initiator, inputs (article ID/title, incident ID, ...), plus a short `summary.md` per session once fetched. **Never read raw `list_sessions` pages into chat** (30-100 KB each): the tool saves them to a file; pass that path to the helper.

- **Refresh:** `list_sessions(pageSize=100)` → `python .github/skills/perception-shared/session_cache.py ingest <saved page file>`. Output `STOP` = the page overlapped the cache (refresh complete) or the depth target was reached; `CONTINUE` = fetch the next page passing the printed `continuationToken` **unchanged**, then `ingest <file> --continue`. Cap a refresh at 10 pages; add `--depth-days N` to go deeper on purpose. An incremental refresh is usually one page.
- **Search:** `search [terms...] [--ti-only] [--articles] [--playbook a,b] [--status succeeded] [--since YYYY-MM-DD]` (all terms must match title/article/summary; `--any` for OR). `need-summary` lists succeeded sessions without a cached summary; fetch each with `get_session_summary` (1-2 KB, free) and store a condensed keyword line with `set <id> --summary-text "..."` (or `--summary-file <file>`; `--no-summary` if it has none). **For several articles use one `set-many <file.json>` call** (write a JSON array of `{"session", "summary", "tiReport"}` with the `create` tool) instead of one `set` per session. `need-summary` returns one session per article (sessions of the same article share intelligence). `coverage` and every search header show how many articles have a cached summary: quote it, because a topic search is only as complete as that number so topic searches can match more than titles.
- **Always state the cache depth** (`covers back to …`, last refresh) in the answer: "no article about X" means "none in the sessions I have seen back to <date>", never "none exist".
- The cache holds IDs and initiator object IDs only on this machine (gitignored); never copy them into tracked files.
- A cached "succeeded" session is a **candidate**, not a result: validate with REFERENCE §5 (`list_outputs`) before presenting anything, and record the outcome with `set <id> --ti-report yes|no`.
## 4. Polling

- Documented lifecycle (Learn tools reference): `status` ∈ `notStarted`/`running`/`succeeded`/`failed`; `statusDetail` ∈ `inProgress`/`waitingForInput`/`completed`/`stopped` (`stop_session` → `failed`/`stopped`). `AgentRun` can carry **`failureInfo { message, errorType }`** — read it first when a run fails. `list_outputs` entries with `readableAsText: false` can only be opened in the Defender portal. `start_session` `method` is documented lowercase (`manual`/`automatic`/`scheduled`); sessions in this tenant display `Manual`. The overview page mentions "continue existing runs with additional instructions", but the published tool list has **no** send-message tool (the 11 tools match what is loaded here), so don't promise follow-up messaging.
- **`stop_session` is permanent** (Learn: a stopped session cannot be resumed or interacted with; work produced so far is kept). Call it only when the user explicitly asks, after confirming; never to "clean up" or because a run is slow.
- Poll **`get_session`** (`status`, `statusDetail`) every few minutes; never tight-loop. Use `Start-Sleep` in chunks of ≤ 5–9 minutes between checks and report progress between them. `statusDetail: waitingForInput` means the session needs a human in the Defender portal (`webUrl`) — report it and stop polling.
- For stage progress use **`list_agent_runs`** (one run per agent: `Main Agent`, `Attack Investigation Agent`, `Threat Intelligence Agent`, `Recon Agent`, `Detection Authoring Agent`, `Posture Prioritization Agent`) — each has `status`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `durationMs`. For detail, `get_agent_run_messages` (newest-first pages; large — only when diagnosing). The session is finished when `get_session.status` is `succeeded`/`failed` **and** all agent runs are terminal; `succeeded` does not guarantee every output file is final, so re-check `list_outputs`.
- Observed runtimes: `investigate-incident` ≈ 15–50 min · `analyze-article` ≈ 4 min · `proactive-protection` ≈ 1 h (TI ≈ 3 → Recon ≈ 14 → Detection Authoring ≈ 29 → Posture ≈ 30 min).
- `summary.md` is a ~30-byte placeholder until the end; it is not progress.

## 5. Validation — **a finished session is not necessarily a useful one**

Earlier MCP versions reported failed runs as `Idle`; on the current version prefer `status` (`failed` is explicit) but **still validate the content** — an agent can finish "successfully" having been unable to access its input. Always, before presenting anything:

1. `get_session_summary`, then `list_outputs`.
2. Require **real report files** (e.g. `report.md`; `threat_intelligence_report*.md`, `detection_report.md`, `prioritization_response.md`, `reconnaissance_report.md`). A lone `summary.md` and/or `*_audit_logs.md` means no analysis was produced.
3. Scan summary and reports for failure language: *could not access*, *failed*, *throttl*, *rate limit*, *not available*, *incomplete*, *did not generate*, *estimated (not measured)*, `BrokenResourceError`, *could not be validated*.
4. Classify the result: **complete**, **partial** (say exactly what is missing), or **failed** (say why, offer a retry).

Known limits worth surfacing when relevant: incidents/alerts older than **30 days** are not accessible to the Attack Investigation Agent; Purview DLP and app-governance alerts, MDE device groups and non-unified-RBAC Sentinel workspaces need extra grants for the agent identity; detection validation can be throttled by the shared Advanced Hunting quota (values then shown as *estimated*, not *measured*).
## 6. Evidence rules

- Perception output is **AI-generated** and **`[asserted]`**, never `[verified]`. Microsoft's own [application card](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/agentic-security/agentic-security-application-card) says agents can produce inaccurate, incomplete or outdated output that depends on the data sources, permissions and input quality, and tells readers to validate it with human judgment; this is the same posture. Tag load-bearing claims `[perception: session <first 8 chars of id>]`.
- **Two kinds of Perception claim; label them differently.** (a) **Tenant observations**: facts Perception read from first-party signal (a resource's configuration, an exposed credential, an install, a sign-in, an indicator seen or not seen). These are high-fidelity, so call them **"Perception-reported"** with the run/snapshot date and **spot-check them automatically** against this repo's own data (see below); once re-confirmed they are `[verified]`, and until then they are `[perception: session <id8>]`, not "unverified" or "doubtful". (b) **Perception's judgments**: ranking, likelihood, impact, TI relevance, a classification, an investigation conclusion. Present these as **"Perception's assessment"**: reasoning to weigh, not a tenant fact. Reserve the bare `[asserted]` tag for claims we could not re-check, or that Perception itself says it could not validate (*coverage gap*). Never blanket a whole report as "asserted and needs confirmation"; say what was spot-checked ("N of M re-confirmed") and what was not.
- A claim becomes `[verified: <table/query>]` only after you re-confirm it with this repo's own queries. **Verification checks run automatically (no approval).** Read-only checks against this tenant are free (Advanced Hunting on analytics tables) and change nothing, so they are part of the job, not an upsell: run bounded Advanced Hunting queries (≤ 30 d, `take`/`summarize`, repo KQL pre-flight, execute before sharing), alert/incident/entity lookups and comparisons with saved repo reports, then label results `[verified: <table>, <window>]` and list in the report what was run. **Still ask first:** anything that costs money (starting any Perception session; Data Lake queries, which are billed and are needed for lookbacks over 30 days), very broad fleet-wide sweeps, and hand-offs that launch another full skill (`user-investigation`, `computer-investigation`, `incident-investigation`…: dozens of queries and their own report: offer them). **Never** change tenant state.
- Disagreements between Perception and this repo's findings are **highlighted for human review, never auto-resolved**. Perception-only findings must be independently queried before being cited as fact.
- Perception's own stated limitations (visibility gaps, "no proof of X") must be carried into the final write-up (*Unable to verify*), not dropped.
- Memory (tenant-context memory files) accelerates interpretation but never replaces collection — see the Memory Is Not Evidence guard.

## 7. Output handling

- Save Perception artifacts **only** under gitignored paths: `reports/perception/` and `temp/perception_sessions.json`. Reports can contain tenant GUIDs, UPNs and hostnames — never write them to tracked files.
- **One subfolder per skill** under `reports/perception/` (create it if missing); never write loose files at the top level:
  | Skill | Folder | Contents |
  |-------|--------|----------|
  | `perception-investigate-attack` | `reports/perception/investigate-attack/` | `incident_<id>_<yyyymmdd>.md` |
  | `perception-triage-alert` | `reports/perception/triage-alert/` | `alert_<id8>_<yyyymmdd>.md` |
  | `perception-protect-against-threat` | `reports/perception/protect-against-threat/<slug>_<yyyymmdd>/` | `report.md` (this skill's report) + one verbatim file per Perception agent report (`threat_intelligence_report.md`, `detection_report.md`, ...) |
  | `perception-extract-threat-intel` | `reports/perception/extract-threat-intel/` | per article: `<slug>_<yyyymmdd>/report.md` + verbatim `threat_intelligence_report.md`; per topic / recent-articles / verification / detection-draft answers: flat `<topic>_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `recent_articles_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `<slug>_verification_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `cd_draft_<slug>_<yyyymmdd>.md` |
  | `perception-tune-detection` | `reports/perception/tune-detection/` | `<slug>_<id8>/` (source `detection_report.md` + `CAND-nnn.{token.txt,kql,rule.json}`), `tune_<candidate>_<slug>_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `tuned_<candidate>_<slug>_<yyyymmdd>.{kql,txt}` |
  Session sources that came from `detect-emerging-threats` (portal-only playbook) go in the consuming skill's folder, named `emerging_<id8>/`.
- Large outputs (> 20 KB) are returned by `read_output` as a saved temp file path; parse with PowerShell/Python rather than pasting into chat. `read_output` takes the **`outputId`** (the `id` from `list_outputs`) plus `sessionId` — not a path.

### 7.1 Attack-graph (mermaid) diagrams

Perception's investigation reports usually contain an **Attack Graph** as a fenced ```` ```mermaid ```` block (observed: exactly one per report, ~10 nodes). Copy it into the saved report instead of dropping it — Mission Control, GitHub and VS Code render it — but **enforce limits**, because some reports carry many or very large diagrams:
- **Copy verbatim, then color it.** Take the block exactly as Perception wrote it, from the freshly read `report.md` (never redraw, rename, reorder or "improve" nodes, edges or labels; never invent a diagram — if the report has none, say so). Perception's raw block has **no styling**, so it renders plain grey here. The **only** permitted additions are `classDef` / `class` lines appended at the end of the fence, using this repo's dark palette (same style as `ai-agent-activity`), so Mission Control renders colors:
  ```
  classDef actor fill:#1e3a5f,stroke:#3b82f6,color:#fff;
  classDef resource fill:#3f3f46,stroke:#a1a1aa,color:#fff;
  classDef artifact fill:#7f1d1d,stroke:#ef4444,color:#fff;
  classDef control fill:#14532d,stroke:#22c55e,color:#fff;
  classDef caution fill:#78350f,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#fff;
  class <ids> <role>;
  ```
  Roles: **actor** = user / app / service principal / agent / workflow; **resource** = cloud resource, service, connector, tool, mailbox, host; **artifact** = file, blob, email, URL, hash, IOC (the thing under suspicion); **control** = security product, detection, alert, block/quarantine action; **caution** = anything Perception marks uncertain or unverified. Assign every node to exactly one role (`class A,B actor;`). Add a one-line legend under the block (*"Colors added for readability: blue = actor, gray = resource, red = artifact, green = control"*). If Perception's block already has its own `classDef`/`style` lines, leave them and add nothing. Node IDs must not be Mermaid keywords (`class`, `style`, `click`, …) — never rename Perception's IDs; if one collides, skip styling and say so. Put the result directly under the verdict as `### Attack graph` with the `[perception: session <id8>]` tag.
- **One diagram per Perception session, only for sessions you present in depth.** Use the primary session's *first* mermaid block (the one under "Attack Graph"). Other mermaid blocks in the same report are **not** embedded.
- **Max 2 diagrams per saved report** (e.g. the primary session plus one cross-checked session). Sessions beyond that are linked (REFERENCE §9), not embedded; say how many diagrams were skipped.
- **Size cap per diagram:** ≤ 60 lines and ≤ ~40 nodes (≤ ~4 KB). Larger ones are not embedded — link the session ("diagram too large to embed — view it in the Defender portal") and, if the user wants it, save it to its own file `reports/perception/<name>_attack_graph.mmd`.
- **Keep it out of chat** unless the user asks: chat answers mention that the saved report includes the graph and where it is; don't paste diagram code into chat.
- **Per-agent reports saved verbatim** (e.g. `reports/perception/protect-against-threat/<slug>_<date>/`) are copies of Perception's files and are exempt from the caps; the caps apply to what *you* write into the report body.
- Don't copy diagrams from the same Perception report into more than one place in the same file (the Appendix should reference the graph shown under the verdict).

## 8. Remediation policy

Perception reports contain "recommended response actions". Re-render them as **portal paths and plain-language steps** (Defender / Entra / Azure portal), per the repo's *Remediation Output Policy*. Never emit state-changing PowerShell, `az` write commands or Graph writes. Perception detections are **proposals**: nothing is deployed by these skills — a human opens the Detection Wizard link and clicks Save.

## 9. Portal links

All `security.microsoft.com` URLs carry `?tid=<tenant_id>` (or `&tid=` when a query string exists) from `config.json`. Incident links: `https://security.microsoft.com/incidents/<ProviderIncidentId>?tid=<tenant_id>`. For the Detection Wizard the `tid` goes **before** the `#` fragment: `…/v2/custom_detection?tid=<tenant_id>#customDetectionRule=<token>`.

**Clickable links in every report and chat answer (mandatory).** Every incident and every Perception session you mention must be a Markdown link — never a bare URL, and never a bare ID:
- **Incident:** `[#<id>](https://security.microsoft.com/incidents/<id>?tid=<tenant_id>)` — always this template; don't substitute other incident URL shapes (e.g. `/incident2/<id>/overview`) even if a tool returns one.
- **Perception session:** `` [`<id8>`](https://security.microsoft.com/perception/session/<full-session-guid>?tid=<tenant_id>) `` — use the `webUrl` returned by `get_session`/`list_sessions` (it already carries `tid`), or build it from the **full** session GUID. Keep the full GUID from the record until the link is written; an 8-character prefix alone cannot be linked.
- Link **every row** of a session table and every prose mention, including the report header and "sessions reviewed" lists. Don't put raw `https://…` text on its own line (`**Session link:** https://…` is wrong; write `**Session:** [`<id8>`](https://…)`).
- **Every report this skill writes MUST open with a dedicated session line within its first 30 lines**, one per Perception session used: `**Perception session:** [🔗 Open session `<id8>` in the Defender portal](<webUrl>) · `<playbook>`, <date/time>, <initiator>`. It is the reader's way back to the source run, so it is never optional, even for a reused or someone else's session. **If no session exists** (nothing found and nothing started), write `**Perception session:** none (<reason>)` instead; `check-links` accepts exactly that. The verbatim copies of Perception's own files stay unmodified (the skill's report links them).
- **Check before you present:** run `python .github/skills/perception-shared/session_cache.py check-links <report.md> --fix`. It fails if the header session line is missing, a session link has no `?tid=`, or a backticked session id is not a link (`--fix` links those from the cache). Exit code 0 is required.
- The evidence tag `[perception: session <id8>]` stays a plain tag (it marks provenance); the session it refers to must be linked at least once in the header.
- Entity identifiers (service principals, apps, blobs, hashes) are not portal objects here — leave them as code text.

## 10. Reading a session: transcript (MCP) vs telemetry (`UnifiedAgentObservability`)

Where the Agent 365 observability connector is enabled, Perception agents (`Global.Microsoft.Defender.*`, channel `PerceptionPlatform`) also appear in the Sentinel Data Lake table `UnifiedAgentObservability` (UAO; query it with `workspaceId: "default"`, `TimeGenerated`). Use the two sources for different jobs. *(Observed in one tenant; not a documented Microsoft contract — re-check when the MCP or connector changes.)*

| Question | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| What did the agent see, run, say and conclude? | **MCP**: `get_agent_run_messages`, `read_output`, `get_session_summary` | UAO carries **no content**: every request/result field is the literal string `Internal` (including replies on `AISpanOutput`). Never answer a content question from UAO or report "no content captured" as a telemetry gap. |
| Did the transcript omit or invent steps? | **UAO** as an integrity check | `EventSessionId` equals the Perception **session GUID**. Per agent, UAO `ExecuteToolBySDK` rows matched the transcript's tool calls one-to-one (names, order, ±1 s). A mismatch is worth flagging. |
| Tenant-wide volume, tokens, model, error rates, which agents ran | **UAO** | One query covers every session; the MCP is per session/run. Per-call input/output tokens and `ModelName` exist only here (the MCP's `Usage` messages are empty). |
| Sub-agent work | MCP `task` calls and results | Sub-tasks are **not** separate agent runs in `list_agent_runs`; in UAO they show only as extra `InferenceCall` rows under the parent agent. |

**Transcript handling (MCP)**
- `get_agent_run_messages` is **newest-first** with a default page of **200** messages; re-sort by `timestamp` and follow `continuationToken` for long runs. A long investigation run can be hundreds of KB — the tool saves large replies to a file; parse them with PowerShell/Python (group by `type`, tally `toolRequest` names) instead of printing them.
- Tool-call **arguments are truncated** (~200 characters, long KQL ends in `...`), so full queries are not recoverable from the transcript; tool **results** are returned in full.
- `list_agent_runs` only lists top-level runs, and its `durationMs` can disagree with the run's own completion message (seen: 7 s listed vs. ~2 h in the transcript). Trust the run's final message and the message timestamps.
- A session can be `succeeded` while the last agent message is a failure (e.g. an authentication error). Read the final messages before trusting status alone.

**Failures**
- UAO records a failed tool call only as `EventErrorDetails` = `Agent operation failed.`; the **real error text is only in the transcript** (`[Tool Error] …`).
- Advanced Hunting calls through the `perception_context` MCP server share a **per-tenant** API quota (observed error: `TooManyRequests … Maximum allowed 45 per 00:01:00 for the key Destination+TenantID`). Because the key is the tenant, concurrent sessions and other Advanced Hunting callers compete; parallel calls inside one session do not predict failure. In one tenant the failure rate was ~15 % at ≤ 35 calls/min tenant-wide, ~23 % at 36–45 and ~36 % at 46–60, plus a ~15 % floor at low load whose cause was not established. Do not call a high `perception_context-RunAdvancedHuntingQuery` failure rate "quota" without sampling transcript error text, and treat a failed query as "no data", never as "no findings".
- When validating or tuning detections, expect the same quota (§5): rerun later rather than concluding a query is broken.
